Transliteration convention: ś = ሠ-series, ʿ = ዐ-series, ə = 6th order, 1st order ä, 4th order a. Translations made fresh from the Geʿez; Dillmann's Lexicon (1865) the lexical aid.
about: Solomon calls his counsellors and proposes that the leading men of Israel send their firstborn sons with his own son to rule Ethiopia, so that his seed will hold three thrones: Israel, Rome and Ethiopia. He cites David's psalms, and the courtiers agree. In chapter 39 the son is anointed in the Holy of Holies, takes the name David, and is blessed by his father. Several words, including the instruments, the acclamation and a few verbs, are uncertain and marked (?).

sentences.i: Chapter 38: How the king took counsel to send his son out with their sons.
sentences.n: Chapter heading. ኀበ here 'where' in `l`, 'how' in `i`, the same loose use as in ch. 37 (?). መከረ 'he took counsel' (perfect, 3rd masc.); ይፈኑ is a subjunctive of ፈነወ 'send', read as 3rd masc. plural 'that they send' (the court does the sending); the same spelling can also be a contracted 3rd sing. 'that he send', so the number is not certain (?). ወልዶ = ወልድ 'son' (accusative) + -ሁ 'his' contracted; ደቂቆሙ = ደቂቅ 'sons' (plural of ወልድ) + -ሆሙ 'their'. ምስለ 'with'. ፴፰ is the numeral 38 (30 + 8).

sentences.l: And-then returned into his-house Solomon king, and-gathered-them to-his-counsellors and-to-his-stewards (?) and-to-elders-of house-of his-kingdom, and-said-to-them: I-was-unable, yes (?), I-say-to-him (?) to-this son;
sentences.i: Then King Solomon went back into his house and gathered his counsellors, his stewards (?) and the elders of his royal household, and said to them: 'I have been unable, yes (?), to say to him (?), to this son;
sentences.n: ወእምዝ 'and then' (ወ- 'and' + እምዝ 'after this'). ገብአ 'he returned' (house entry). ወአስተጋብኦሙ 'and he gathered them': ወ- + አስተጋብአ (causative-tä stem of ተጋብአ 'assemble') + -ሆሙ 'them'. ለመማክርቲሁ 'to his counsellors' (`l` keeps the literal ለ- 'to'; it marks the object here: 'gathered them, his counsellors'), then መማክርት (plural of መምከር, the glossary lemma; the singular is not confirmed) + -ሁ. ወለመገብቱ: መገብት is uncertain to me (?), perhaps 'stewards, those in charge of provisions'. ለመላህቅተ ቤተ መንግሥቱ 'the elders of the house of his kingdom': መላህቅት 'elders' in the construct before ቤተ 'house-of' before መንግሥቱ 'kingdom-his'. ስእንኩ 'I was unable' (ስእነ, 1st sing. perfect); ኦሆ 'yes, indeed' (?). አብሎቶ is a crux (?): the shape fits a 1st-sing. imperfect እብል of ብህለ 'say' + -ሎ 'to him', written አብሎ-, with the final -ቶ unexplained (the house entry); it is not a verbal noun, which would be ብሂሎ. I read ስእንኩ with an asyndetic complement, 'I was unable to say to him', and ለዝንቱ ወልድ 'to this son' repeating the suffix. The sense is a guess from context (ch. 37, where the son insists on leaving): Solomon admits he could not turn the son from going (?).

sentences.i: And now hear what I tell you: come, let us make him king over the land of Ethiopia, together with your sons who sit at my right hand and my left. In the same way let your elder sons sit at his right hand and his left;
sentences.n: ወይእዜኒ 'and now' (ወይእዜ + the emphatic particle -ኒ). ስምዑኒ 'hear me' (imperative plural + -ኒ 'me'). ዘእነግረክሙ 'that which I tell you' (ዘ- 'that which' + እነግር 'I tell' + -ክሙ 'you pl.'). ሀቡ is the plural imperative of ሀበ 'give', used as an exhortation, 'come now' (?); it is followed by ናንግሦ 'let us make him king' (1st-plural cohortative of አንገሠ, the causative of ነግሠ 'reign'; ና- is the 1cp causative prefix). ለብሔረ ኢትዮጵያ: ለ- here introduces the land over which he is to rule; ብሔረ is the construct 'land-of'. እለ ትነብሩ is 'who sit' with a 2nd-plural verb after a 3rd-plural antecedent, a slip or a looseness in the printed text (?). በየማንየ 'at my right hand' (በ- 'at, in' + የማን 'right' + -የ 'my'), ወበፀጋምየ 'and at my left'; sitting at the right and left is the place of counsellors and heirs. ከማሁ 'likewise'. ይንበሩ is jussive.

sentences.i: and all of you, counsellors and nobles, come, let us give your firstborn sons, and we will have two kingdoms. I shall serve (?) here with you, and our sons will reign there;
sentences.n: ወኵልክሙ 'and all of you' (ኵሉ 'all' + -ክሙ). መኳንንት 'nobles, governors'. ነሀብ is the cohortative 'let us give', parallel to ሀቡ. በኵረ 'firstborn' (accusative; the plural sense 'firstborn ones' is taken from context). ክልኤ መንግሥት 'two kingdoms'. ወአንሰ 'and as for me' (-ሰ contrastive). እትለአክ is difficult (?): from ተለአከ, which gives 'I shall be sent' or 'I shall serve'; 'I shall serve' (?) follows the grammar; 'stay', which an earlier draft used, would be only a guess. ወደቂቅነሂ 'and our sons also' (-ሂ 'also'). በሂየ is a variant spelling of በህየ 'there', kept as printed.

sentences.i: And thirdly, I hope in God that he will give me offspring, and that I will have a third king.
sentences.n: ወሣልሰኒ 'and thirdly' (ሣልስ 'third' + -ኒ). እሴፈዎ 'I hope in him' (ሴፈወ 'hope, expect', with -ኦ 'him'; ለእግዚኣብሔር 'in/of God' repeats the object). ከመ የሀበኒ 'that he give me' (ከመ + 3ms of ወሀበ + -ኒ; the prefix is spelled የ- for ይ- before the laryngeal, as in የኀሥሥ in the previous unit, so I take it as the subjunctive ይሀብ). ዘርአ 'seed, offspring'. ሊተ 'to me' is the independent dative form. ሣልሰ ንጉሠ: ንጉሠ is the accusative 'a king', the accusative in -ä marking the predicate. This is Solomon's hope for a further heir from the Roman alliance described next.

sentences.i: For Baltasor, the king of Rome, seeks that I give my son to his daughter, and that he install him as king for me, with his daughter, over all the city of Rome;
sentences.n: እስመ 'for, because'. የኀሥሥ 'he seeks' (ኀሠሠ). በልጣሶር is the king's name as printed (a Roman king's name; I give it as printed and make no identification). ንጉሠ ሮሜ 'king of Rome': ንጉሥ in the construct, with the case-vowel ä. ከመ አሀቦ 'that I give him' (1st-sing. subjunctive of ሀበ); ወልድየ 'my son' (ወልድ + -የ). ለወለቱ 'to his daughter' (ለ- + ወለት 'daughter' + -ሁ). ወያንግሦ 'and (that) he make him king' (3rd masc. subject, Baltasor). ሊተ 'for me'. ሀገረሮሜ is printed as one word, ሀገረ ሮሜ 'city-of Rome'. The 'my son' here is another son of Solomon, distinct from the one who is leaving.

sentences.i: for he has no child except her, and he has sworn that he will make no one king except one from the seed of David my father;
sentences.n: አልቦውሉደ is printed as one word, አልቦ ውሉደ 'there is no offspring'. ዘርአ ዘእንበሌሃ 'seed apart from her' (ዘእንበለ 'without, except' + -ሃ 'her'). ወመሐለ 'and he swore'. ከመ ኢያንግሥ 'that he not make king' (negative subjunctive). ዘእንበለ እምዘርአ ዳዊት 'except from the seed of David'; እም- 'from' is the proclitic. Solomon here describes his own line as the only acceptable royal line, even to a foreign king; the theme of David's seed as the covenanted dynasty (2 Samuel 7:12-16) runs through the passage.

sentences.l: And-Jeroboam-also shall-reign here over Israel, for thus (is) his-prophecy to-David my-father: will-be his-seed, of-Solomon, 3 heads-of kingdom upon earth.
sentences.i: And Jeroboam also shall reign here over Israel, for so is the prophecy to David my father: Solomon's seed will be three chief seats of kingship upon the earth.
sentences.n: ወኢዮርብዓምኒ: Jeroboam (ኢዮርብዓም) is kept as printed. In the Bible Jeroboam was a northern rival, and Solomon's heir was Rehoboam (ሮብዓም); the text uses the name for the heir who stays in Israel, as a name of the line (?). I follow the printed text. ይነግሥ 'he shall reign'. ዝየ 'here'. ትንቢቱ ለዳዊት 'his prophecy to David' (ትንቢት 'prophecy'). ፫ is the numeral 3, 'spoken' ሠለስቱ; here it stands before አርእስተ 'heads-of' (construct of ርእስ 'head'), so 'three heads of kingship', that is three throne-lines: Israel, Rome, Ethiopia. The prophecy is not a verse I can identify in David's writings; it is the text's own claim of a promise to David.

sentences.i: Let us send priests to them, and let us establish laws for them, so that they worship and serve (?) the God of Israel in the chief seats of kingship, and that God may be praised among the kindred of his people Israel and be exalted in all the earth.
sentences.n: ወንፌኑ 'and let us send' (cohortative). ሎሙ 'to them'. ካህናተ 'priests' (accusative plural). ወንሥራዕ ሎሙ ሕገጋተ 'and let us establish laws for them' (ሠርዐ 'establish, ordain'; ሕግ plural ሕገጋት). ወያምልኩ ወይግነዩ 'and they will worship and bow/serve' (ገነየ 'bow down, serve'; the exact nuance is (?)), subjunctive continuing the cohortative. ለአምላከ እስራኤል 'to the God of Israel' (አምላከ is the construct 'God-of'). ወይሴባሕ 'and he will be praised': the passive of ሰብሐ, subject እግዚኣብሔር. በዘመደ ሕዝቡ 'among the kinsfolk of his people' (ዘመድ 'kin'). ወይትሌዐል 'and he will be exalted' (ተለዐለ). The hope that God be praised among all the earth echoes Psalm 57:5 and 108:5, 'be exalted above the heavens; let your glory be over all the earth' (?).

sentences.n: በከመ 'as, just as'. ጸሐፈ 'he wrote'; አቡየ 'my father' (አብ + -የ) is David, and መጽሐፉ 'his book' is the Psalter. እንዘ ይብል 'saying' (እንዘ + imperfect = a circumstantial 'while he says'). በልዎሙ ለአሕዛብ 'say to them, to the nations': the plural imperative of ብህለ 'say' takes the pronoun -ሙ and then ለአሕዛብ 'to the nations'. ነግሠ 'has reigned'. sentences.l: His-praise in assembly-of his-righteous. Let-rejoice Israel in his-maker; for-us is glory-of-kingdom, and-let-us-praise our-maker, and-will-see us nations who worship idols, and-fear us and-make-us-king and-praise God and-fear him.
sentences.i: "His praise is in the assembly of his righteous ones; let Israel rejoice in his Maker." The glory of kingship is ours, and let us praise our Maker, and the nations who worship idols will see us, and fear us, and make us kings, and praise God and fear him.
sentences.n: The first clause echoes Psalm 149:1-2: 'his praise in the assembly of the faithful... let Israel rejoice in his Maker.' ስብሐቲሁ 'his praise' (ስብሐት + -ሁ). በማኅበረ ጻድቃኑ 'in the assembly of his righteous ones' (በ- 'in', ማኅበረ construct, ጻድቃን 'righteous' + -ሁ). ይትፌሣሕ 'let him rejoice' (ተፈሥሐ). በፈጣሪሁ 'in his Maker' (ፈጣሪ 'creator'). From ለነ ይእቲ 'ours is it' the text is Solomon's own comment: ክብረመንግሥት is printed as one word, ክብረ መንግሥት 'glory of kingship' (the book's title phrase ክብረ ነገሥት 'glory of kings' is related). ኪያነ 'us' (accusative independent pronoun). እለ ያመልኩ ጣዖተ 'who worship idols' (ጣዖት, accusative plural form ጣዖተ). The two last verbs, ይፍርሁነ and ይፍርህዎ, are 'fear us' and 'fear him'; ያንግሡነ 'make us kings'. The idea that nations will acknowledge Israel is the text's own application of the psalms.

sentences.i: They brought him into the Holy of Holies. He took hold of the horns of the altar, and the kingdom was given him by the mouth of Zadok the priest and by the mouth of Joash the priest, the messenger of King Solomon's might (?), and he anointed him with the holy perfumed oil for kingship;
sentences.n: ወአብእዎ 'and they brought him in' (አብአ, causative of ቦአ 'enter'). ቅድስተ ቅዱሳን 'Holy of Holies' (ቅድስት 'holy place' in the construct before ቅዱሳን 'holy ones'): the royal consecration is set in the Temple's inner shrine. ተእኅዘ 'he was seized, held' or 'took hold'; በአቅርንተ ምሥዋዕ 'by the horns of the altar' (ቀርን, plural አቅርንት). The 'horns of the altar' are those of Exodus 27:2 and 1 Kings 1:50, where Adonijah seizes them; here it is a sacred place of ritual (?). ወተውህቦ መንግሥት 'and was given him kingdom' (ተውህበ passive of ሀበ + -ኦ). በአፈ 'by the mouth of' (አፍ 'mouth' construct, አፈ). ሳዶቅ ካህን is Zadok the priest, as in 1 Kings 1:39. ኢዮአስ ካህን 'Joash the priest' is not identified to me (?). መልአከ ኀይሉ ለንጉሥ ሰሎሞን is read as a title of Joash with the anticipatory genitive found elsewhere in this text (ዘርኡ ለሰሎሞን, ውሉዶ ለአቡየ ዳዊት): 'messenger of his might, of King Solomon', that is 'messenger of King Solomon's might' (?). ወቀብኦ 'and he anointed him' (ቀብአ, 3rd masc. SING. + -ኦ): the subject is unexpressed, presumably Zadok (cf. 1 Kings 1:39) (?). እምነ ቅዱስ ቅብአ ዕፍረት 'from the holy oil of perfume' (እምነ 'from', partitive; English says 'with') (ቅብእ 'oil, ointment').

sentences.i: He went out from the house of God, and they gave him the name David, because by law the name of king had come to him;
sentences.n: ወወፅአ 'and he went out' (ወፅአ). እምነ ቤተ እግዚኣብሔር 'from the house of God': እምነ is a variant of እም- 'from' with the added -ነ. ወሰመይዎ ስሞ ዳዊት 'and they named him, his name (being) David': ሰመየ + -ኦ 'named him', with the name as a second object, ስሞ 'his name'. This means the son takes the regnal name David, in the line of the royal ancestor of Psalms. In Ethiopian tradition Menelik is crowned as David II. እስመ በሕግ ረከቦ ስመ ንጉሥ 'because by law the name of king found him': ረከቦ is ረከበ 'find, befall' with -ኦ 'him' already as its object, so ስመ ንጉሥ is read as its subject and not as a second object (?).

sentences.i: They mounted him on King Solomon's mule and led him around the city, saying: 'We have appointed you from here on (?).'
sentences.n: ወአጽዐንዎ 'and they mounted him' (አጽዐነ, causative of ጸዐነ 'carry', so 'made him ride'). ዲበ 'upon'. በቅል 'mule', the animal of kings in 1 Kings 1:33 (where Solomon rides King David's mule). Here too the mule is the king's, and the procession echoes Solomon's own ride. ወአዖድዎ ሀገረ 'and they led him around the city' (አዖደ, causative of ዐወደ 'go around'; ሀገረ accusative). እንዘ ይብሉ 'saying'. ሤምናከ 'we appointed you' (ሠየመ 'appoint', 1st plural perfect + -ከ 'you'). እምዝየ 'from here' (?), perhaps 'from now'.

sentences.i: And there are some who say: 'It is right and fitting for him: from the river of Egypt to the west of the sun, let Ethiopia be your appointed realm; blessed be your descendants upon the earth, and from ሴዋ (?) in the south to the sunrise of India (?), whatever pleases them (?);
sentences.n: ወቦ እለ ይብሉ 'and there are those who say' (ቦ 'there is'). ርቱዕ 'right', ይደልዎ 'it befits him' (ደለወ 'be fitting' + -ኦ). እምፈለገ ግብጽ 'from the river of Egypt' (እም- + ፈለገ construct, 'river-of'); compare Genesis 15:18, 'from the river of Egypt', as the edge of the promised land. እስከ ምዕራበ ፀሐይ 'to the west of the sun', sunset. ሢመትከ 'your office, rule', with ኢትዮጵያ 'Ethiopia'. ቡሩክ ዘርእከ 'blessed (be) your seed' (ቡሩክ 'blessed'). ወእምሴዋ is uncertain (?): perhaps a place-name ሴዋ; ደቡባዊ 'southern'. ሠረቀ ህንድ 'the rising of India' (ሠረቀ taken as a noun 'sunrise' in the construct, though the house entry has the 3ms perfect 'it rose'; 'until it rose on India' is the verbal alternative) (?); India stands at the east edge of the stretch. ዘታሠምሮን is hard (?): 'what you please them with' or 'what pleases them'; ታሠምሮን could be 2nd masc. or 3rd fem. with -ሆን 'them (fem.)'. The long boundaries claim Africa's whole breadth for the new king.

sentences.i: May all your enemies and haters be subdued (?) before you, and may there be wholeness and ኳላ (?) for you and your descendants after you; you will rule many peoples, but no one will rule you.'
sentences.n: ይኩኑከ 'may they be to you'. ግሩራነ is uncertain (?): I read 'cowed, subdued' by guess; ኵሎሙ ፀርከ ወጸላእትከ 'all your enemies and your haters' (ፀር, ጸላኢ, plural ጸላእት). በቅድሜከ 'before you'. ፍጽመ 'perfection, completeness'; ኳላ I do not know (?), perhaps 'support' or 'measure'. እምድኅሬከ 'after you'. ወትኴንን 'and you will rule' (ኰነነ 'judge, rule'); ብዙኃነ አሕዛበ 'many peoples'. ወለከሰ 'but as for you' (ለከ + -ሰ); ዘይኴንነከ 'who would rule you'. The wish for the king to rule nations and none to rule him closely matches Deuteronomy 15:6 ('you shall rule over many nations, but they shall not rule over you'); compare also Isaac's blessing, Genesis 27:29 (?). ኳላ is left unrendered in `i`.
